title: Perfect State Transfer on Oriented Circulant Graphs: A Complete Classification
abstract: The continuous-time quantum walk on an oriented circulant graph is determined by the Fourier eigenvalues of its Hermitian adjacency matrix. We classify perfect state transfer (PST) between distinct vertices in every nonempty oriented circulant graph. We show that each such graph is described by an odd primitive quadratic Dirichlet character of conductor $Δ$, a set of gcd-classes, and a choice between the two orientations of each selected class. For a graph of order $n$, we derive an explicit formula for every Fourier eigenvalue without assuming that $n/Δ$ is coprime to $Δ$. We prove that PST occurs only for $Δ\in\{3,4,8\}$ and give necessary and sufficient conditions on the connection set for each conductor. Equivalently, the square-free radicands of oriented circulant graphs with PST are exactly $1$, $2$, and $3$. More generally, when $λ_j=\sqrt{D}η_j$ with $η_j\in\mathbb{Z}$, congruences satisfied by the integers $η_j$ determine all PST pairs and times, the minimum period, and the largest vertex sets supporting multiple state transfer (MST). In this class, pretty good state transfer is equivalent to PST. We also determine the connected orders and enumerate the resulting graphs.
summary: This paper rigorously classifies all oriented circulant graphs that support Perfect State Transfer (PST) during a continuous-time quantum walk. By employing advanced number theory involving quadratic Dirichlet characters, the authors prove that PST can only occur if the graph's underlying structure is determined by conductors $\Delta \in \{3, 4, 8\}$. This provides a complete mathematical blueprint for realizing such quantum transport phenomena.
main_problem: The primary goal is to classify all oriented circulant graphs that exhibit Perfect State Transfer (PST) between distinct vertices.
main_result: PST in these graphs is strictly limited to cases where the graph's structure is governed by conductors $\Delta \in \{3, 4, 8\}$, which corresponds to square-free radicands of 1, 2, and 3.
method: The classification uses advanced number theory, specifically properties of odd primitive quadratic Dirichlet characters and Fourier analysis applied to the graph's Hermitian adjacency matrix spectrum.
model_or_system: The model is a continuous-time quantum walk on an oriented circulant graph $	ext{Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_n, C)$. The dynamics are governed by the Hamiltonian derived from the graph's Hermitian adjacency matrix $A$.
key_observables: Perfect State Transfer (PST) and Multiple State Transfer (MST), which depend directly on the Fourier eigenvalues of the adjacency matrix.
important_parameters: The conductor $\Delta$ of the underlying quadratic Dirichlet character, and the graph order $n$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the graph is finite and simple, relying heavily on number theoretic tools related to characters and gcd-classes.
figures_summary: Table 2 provides a comprehensive classification summarizing representative graphs exhibiting PST, categorized by their conductor $\Delta$, square-free radicand $\delta$, order $n$, and counts of specific transfer cardinalities ($h$).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing spectral properties using quadratic characters (Section 2), deriving general state transfer theorems from the spectrum (Section 3), and finally applying these constraints to restrict the possible conductors ($\Delta$) to complete the classification (Section 4).
why_interesting: This work provides a deep mathematical characterization of quantum transport phenomena on structured graphs, which has direct implications for designing quantum communication channels or quantum simulators based on lattice structures.
